🇭🇰 HONG KONG REOPENS AFTER RAGASA - THE YEAR’S BIGGEST CYCLONE

Hong Kong just staggered back online after 36 hours frozen by Ragasa, the planet’s most powerful storm of 2025.

Flights resumed at dawn, with the airport scrambling to process 1,000+ flights in 2 days. 

Businesses, transport, and some schools reopened - though kindergartens stayed shut under Typhoon Signal 3.

The storm’s toll: 14 dead across the Philippines and Taiwan, 100+ injured in Hong Kong, and roads collapsed, 1,000+ trees down, 85 floods reported. 

Seawater even smashed into the Fullerton hotel, flooding its glass-front lobby.

Markets felt it too: empty supermarket shelves, spiking veggie prices, and traders eyeing supply chain delays. 

Ragasa didn’t just drown roads - it shook Asia’s logistics hub.

For a city built on finance and speed, 36 hours offline is a gut check: what happens when the world’s dealmakers can’t get to the table - or off the island?

Source: Reuters

🚨12 HOUR NEWS RECAP

1.⁠ Joshua Jahn opened fire on an ICE facility in Dallas from a rooftop before killing himself. The attack killed one detainee and wounded two others, but no ICE officers were injured.

2.⁠ Denmark called up the EU and NATO after hostile drones shut down Aalborg airport and 3 others. The government hasn’t yet pulled the Article 4 lever - that’s NATO’s emergency huddle clause - but it’s on the table.

3.⁠ Trump removed Biden’s official White House portrait and replaced it with a framed image of the autopen - the machine that signed documents in his name.

4.⁠ Hong Kong staggered back online after 36 hours frozen by Ragasa, the planet’s most powerful storm of 2025. It left 14 dead across the Philippines and Taiwan, 100+ injured in Hong Kong, and roads collapsed, 1,000+ trees down, and 85 floods reported.

5.⁠ Marine Le Pen is seizing on Macron’s chaos as his fifth PM in 2 years, Sebastien Lecornu, struggles to form a functioning government. The National Rally party is now openly demanding snap elections, betting that Macron’s paralysis - and Lecornu’s shaky budget math - will only deepen public frustration.

6.⁠ Trump is set to finalize a deal transferring TikTok’s U.S operations to a joint venture of American investors later today, with ByteDance holding under 20%. Oracle will oversee U.S user data and retrain TikTok’s algorithm to prevent outside manipulation.

7.⁠ Several Antifa members were arrested and charged after surrounding an ICE building in Eugene, Oregon. It marks the first time Antifa members have been charged as domestic terrorists, following Trump’s order designating the group a terror organization.

8.⁠ Lindsey Halligan, just one week into her new job as Acting U.S Attorney for Eastern Virginia, wants to indict former FBI Director James Comey for allegedly lying to Congress about Russiagate. She is expected to take the case to a grand jury next week.

9.⁠ William Shatner was rushed to the hospital after a blood sugar emergency at his Los Angeles home. Sources say he’s now “resting comfortably” and “doing good” - but at nearly a century old, every health scare feels like a red alert for Trekkies.

10.⁠ A Paris court convicted former French President Nicolas Sarkozy of conspiracy tied to alleged Libyan financing of his 2007 campaign. He was acquitted on charges of corruption, concealment of embezzled funds, and illegal campaign financing.
